subject: PayGrid model fit eval \u2014 parity discussion
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid model fit eval — parity discussion

Hi Tom — great call earlier, thanks for walking us through the payflows demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

Summary of today's takeaways:
- Primary goal: match PayGrid's current proprietary baseline on (1) intent classification and (2) response generation quality for customer support scenarios.
- Target acceptance thresholds you mentioned: ~95% intent accuracy and human-preferred responses >= baseline in A/B blind tests.
- Dataset: ~12k anonymized historical interactions (you said security signoff pending).

Redwood recommended model slate for the eval (starting tier):
1) redwood-open-13B-quant (faster, lower cost)
2) llama2-13b-refined (competitive open baseline)
3) redwood-30b-intl (if latency budget allows — stronger few-shot generalization)

Proprietary baseline we understand you're benchmarking against: PayGrid-Prod-Baseline (internal) — we'll treat that as the control in blind pairwise tests.

Planned evals and artifacts we'll produce:
- Metric sheet with intent accuracy, F1 by label, BLEU/ROUGE for canned responses, and a human preference column. (link to drive + CSV)
- Prompt set v2 (we'll run canonical prompts + edge-case prompts you flagged).
- Parity checklist: top 10 failure modes to watch.

Acceptance criteria proposal (please confirm):
- Intent accuracy >= 95% OR within 1.5 points of your baseline and no significant regression on top-3 high-priority intents.
- Human blind-preference: open model chosen >= 40% of the time vs baseline in a 300-sample panel.

Next steps / timeline:
1) We need the anonymized dataset + SSO for access to sample logs (security review) — you mentioned Asha would coordinate.
2) Redwood runs a scoped fitter/benchmark (2 weeks) and publishes the drive results + eval plan.
3) Joint sync to review parity decisions and discuss rollout implications (tentative: Oct 14).

Attachments: paygrid-prompt-set-v2.json (sample prompts), paygrid-eval-plan.pdf (high-level plan). Full benchmark outputs will be shared in the drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_paygrid_benchmarks

Thanks — looping in Marissa and Marcus to own the eval execution.

— Lauren Bishop
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Tom Alvarez <tom@paygrid.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Singh <asha@paygrid.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 17:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval — parity discussion

Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Acceptance thresholds — the 95% intent accuracy is what our product team would prefer, but we can be pragmatic if you show clear cost/latency benefits and no regression on our top-3 intents (payment_failure, refund_request, chargeback).
2) Human blind-preference: 300 samples sounds right. Can we make sure those include a fair mix of short/long dialogs?
3) Security — Asha will follow up with the PoC checklist. We expect a SOC2 attestation and a narrow, pre-approved S3 snapshot.

On timeline: Oct 14 sync works for the decision meeting. Would like an interim status update week of Oct 6.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Head of ML Ops, PayGrid
tom@paygrid.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval — parity discussion

Adding our internal execution plan and owners — quoted original below for context.

Plan (internal):
- Day 0-2: ingest sample S3 snapshot (anonymized) and run data quality checks. Owners: Marissa (lead), Marcus (infra).
- Day 3-8: run baseline generation across three model candidates (redwood-open-13B-quant, llama2-13b-refined, redwood-30b-intl). We'll standardize prompts from paygrid-prompt-set-v2.json. Owner: Marissa.
- Day 9-12: collect automated metrics (intent acc, F1 per label, token cost/latency), generate paygrid-benchmark-results.csv. Owner: Marcus.
- Day 13-14: human evaluation panel (300 samples) + blind-preference scoring. Owner: aditya_rao (we'll run the annotation UI).

Key QA / parity checks we'll run:
- Intent stratification by frequency buckets (top-3 emphasis).
- Regression tracking: automated diff vs PayGrid-Prod-Baseline. Flag if drop > 1.5 points on top intents.
- Cost/latency: per-token cost and 95th percentile latency on your latency SLO.

Deliverables to customer (by Oct 6 interim):
- Interim metrics dashboard + partial benchmark CSV (paygrid-benchmark-results.csv)
- Annotator guidelines and sample blind test UI link

Attachments: paygrid-benchmark-results.csv (partial), paygrid-eval-plan.pdf (updated).

On the acceptance criteria: we recommend keeping the dual rule (absolute threshold OR no-regression + cost benefit). That gives PayGrid flexibility to pick a cost-savvy drop-in.

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval — parity discussion

Thanks team — Tom and Asha, appreciated. Confirming next steps and owners:

- PayGrid: Asha to share S3 snapshot + security checklist by EOD Sep 30.
- Redwood: Marissa will kick off ingestion once snapshot is available, Marcus will provision inference jobs, Aditya will set up the human eval panel. Interim update the week of Oct 6, final parity review Oct 14.

We will also include a short section in the interim deliverable that calls out the top 5 failure modes and recommended mitigations (prompt engineering, per-intent reranking, or a small supervised classifier fallback).

If anything shifts on your side re: timeline/security, please flag ASAP — we can adjust the schedule but will aim to keep the Oct 14 decision sync.

— Lauren
